;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen]], [[Saudi Arabian–Yemeni border conflict (2015–present)|Saudi Arabian–Yemeni border conflict]]
**Saudi state news agency [[Saudi Press Agency|SPA]] says [[Saudi Armed Forces]] shot down an explosive-laden [[unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drone]] launched against Saudi territory from [[Al Hudaydah Governorate]], on [[Yemen]]'s [[Red Sea]] coast. The [[Houthis]] report a Saudi air strike on [[Saada Governorate]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security-saudi/saudi-coalition-says-it-shot-down-houthi-drone-heading-for-kingdom-idUSKCN2521FX (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**The [[Economy of the Philippines|Philippine economy]] falls into [[recession]] for the first time in 29 years after the economy shrank by 16.5% in the April to June quarter from the same period last year, which is the biggest slump in the government's quarterly [[GDP]] data dating back to 1981. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/business/philippine-economy-dives-into-recession-in-worst-slump-on-record-12994870 (CNA)]
*[[China–United States trade war]]
**Invoking the [[International Emergency Economic Powers Act]], [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] issues several [[executive order]]s barring firms and American citizens from trading and doing financial transactions with [[China|Chinese]] technology companies [[ByteDance]] and [[Tencent]], effectively banning their respective apps [[TikTok]] and [[WeChat]] within the [[United States]]. The orders are set to go into effect in 45 days. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/us-usa-wechat-trump/trump-issues-bans-on-chinas-tiktok-wechat-stoking-tension-with-beijing-idUKKCN25304R (Reuters)]
*[[First Trump tariffs|Trump tariffs]]
**Trump implements a [[tariff]] of 10% on aluminum imports from [[Canada]], pursuant to Section 232 of the US [[Trade Expansion Act]]. The [[United States]] previously imposed tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminum in 2018 citing national security concerns, before removing them last year as part of the [[United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement|USCMA Free Trade Agreement]]. [[Prime Minister of Canada]] [[Justin Trudeau]] vows "dollar-for-dollar" countermeasures. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/trump-aluminum-tariff-1.5677036 (CBC)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Beirut explosions]], [[2019–2020 Lebanese protests]]
**Security forces fired tear gas to disperse dozens of anti-government protesters in [[Beirut]] calling for the Lebanese government's resignation near the parliament building. Several people were wounded in the clashes. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/lebanon-orders-house-arrest-officials-beirut-blast-live-200805230752876.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****The [[Robert Koch Institute]] reports 1,045 new cases in Germany during the last 24 hours. It is the first time since May 7 that the number of new [[COVID-19]] cases in the country has surpassed 1,000. [https://www.newindianexpress.com/world/2020/aug/06/germany-records-1045-fresh-coronavirus-cases-highest-in-three-months-2179934.html (''The New Indian Express'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
****[[Poland]] reports a record 726 new cases during the last 24 hours, and the government will impose limits on restaurants, sporting events, public transport and weddings in 19 of its 380 counties as of Saturday, August 8. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-08-06/poland-imposes-virus-restrictions-in-most-affected-counties (Bloomberg)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports 1,318 new COVID-19 cases during the last 24 hours, a record high for a second consecutive day. [https://www.unian.info/society/covid-19-in-ukraine-another-record-spike-in-new-cases-reported-on-aug-6-11102780.html (UNIAN)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] reports 904 new COVID-19 deaths in the last 24 hours, which is the largest number of fatalities in a single-day as new cases reach 56,000. [https://english.jagran.com/india/record-56282-new-covid19-cases-in-last-24-hours-take-indias-tally-to-1964-lakh-death-toll-tops-40000-check-statewise-list-here-10014916 (''Jagran English'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] reports 3,561 new COVID-19 cases on which inching the total tally closer to 120,000 and causing the country to overtake [[Indonesia]] as the Southeast Asian nation with the most number of infections. [https://rappler.com/nation/coronavirus-cases-philippines-august-6-2020 (Rappler)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Melbourne]] enters Stage 4 lockdown, which is Australia's toughest lockdown yet, following a spike of COVID-19 cases within the city and surrounding [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200806-melbourne-enters-australia-s-toughest-virus-lockdown (France24)]

;International relations
*[[Belarus–United States relations]], [[2020 Belarusian presidential election]]
**[[President of Belarus|Belarusian President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] says security forces have arrested "a number of" U.S. citizens, just days before the country goes to the polls for a [[2020 Belarusian presidential election|presidential election]]. In the speech, Lukashenko claims Belarus is the victim of a "hybrid war", and that "we should expect dirty tricks from any side". [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-belarus-election/belarus-says-u-s-nationals-detained-before-presidential-election-idUKKCN2521LK?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Egypt–Greece relations]]
**[[Egypt]] and [[Greece]] sign a bilateral agreement which establishes a new [[exclusive economic zone]] (EEZ) in the [[Eastern Mediterranean]] between the two countries. The agreement prompts anger from [[Turkey]], with the Turkish Foreign Ministry describing the deal as "null and void". [https://www.ekathimerini.com/255573/gallery/ekathimerini/news/greece-and-egypt-sign-agreement-on-exclusive-economic-zone (''Ekathimerini'')] [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/greece-egypt-violate-turkeys-libyas-rights/1934121 (Anadolu Agency)]

;Law and crime
*[[Canada–China relations]]
**A court in [[China]] sentences a [[Canada|Canadian]] man [[Capital punishment in China|to death]] on drug charges. His alleged accomplice receives [[life imprisonment]]. Police had confiscated 120 kilograms (266 pounds) of [[ketamine]] from the defendant's home. He is the third Canadian citizen to receive the death sentence for drug smuggling since Canadian authorities arrested [[Huawei]] executive [[Meng Wanzhou]] in late 2018 on an extradition request from the [[United States]]. [https://apnews.com/7569c5df2c3f32f92e57a7771cef660a (AP)]
*Two security alerts are triggered in [[Belfast]] aimed at the newly formed [[East Belfast GAA]] team. The bomb threats are later deemed as hoaxes aiming to destabilize the team which is aiming to bring together both sides of the political divide. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-northern-ireland-53686763 (BBC News)]
*Former [[Ministry of Interior (Saudi Arabia)|Saudi Ministry of the Interior]] official [[Saad bin Khalid Al Jabry]] accuses [[Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia|Crown Prince]] [[Mohammed bin Salman]] of attempting to assassinate him in Canada, where he currently lives in exile, two weeks after the [[Assassination of Jamal Khashoggi|assassination]] of dissident journalist [[Jamal Khashoggi]]. The would-be assassins, believed to be the [[Tiger Squad]], were stopped at [[Toronto Pearson International Airport]] after Canadian border officials became suspicious of them following interviews. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-53677869 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Mauritania]]n President [[Mohamed Ould Ghazouani]] appoints public administrator [[Mohamed Ould Bilal]] as [[Prime Minister of Mauritania|Prime Minister]] after the government of previous Prime Minister [[Ismail Ould Bedde Ould Cheikh Sidiya]] resigned hours earlier. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/mauritania-names-pm-previous-cabinet-resigns-200806134516924.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Ministry of Defense (Peru)|Minister of Defense]] of [[Peru]] [[Walter Martos]] is named the new [[Prime Minister of Peru|Prime Minister]] after the approval of the motion of no-confidence against [[Pedro Cateriano]]. [https://www.expreso.com.pe/politica/walter-martos-cateriano-premier-presidente-consejo-ministros/ (Expreso)]

;Science and technology
*[[Twitter]] says it will label [[state media]], official government accounts and their staff. State-funded media outlets with "editorial independence", such as the [[National Public Radio]] in the U.S., or [[BBC]] in the UK, will not be among those labelled, according to a spokesman for the [[social media]] site. [https://reuters.com/article/uk-twitter-labels-media/twitter-labels-state-media-government-officials-accounts-idUKKCN2522E6?il=0 (Reuters)]
